name: Shiva Published Studies (3 amygdala + 3 chirp configurations, Swann 2002 timing)
origin: Todd Murphy (Shiva software, 'Published Experiment Session'), modelled on the Laurentian circumcerebral protocol (Cook, Koren & Persinger 1999; Richards, Koren & Persinger 2002; Persinger, Roll, Tiller, Koren & Cook 2002, the Ingo Swann study)
summary: Murphy's Shiva session after the six configurations of the Persinger lab's psi studies: three with the amygdala signal, then three with a chirp, counter-clockwise around the head, with 2-min quiet intervals, 40 min. Step times, point durations and gaps follow Table 1 in the lab's Swann paper (Persinger 2002); that the Shiva session uses them is this project's inference. Murphy calls it a good session to begin with.
notes: Murphy: 'The first three use the amygdala signal, and the second three use the chirp signal. There are quiet intervals between them' (experiment_signals.htm). He publishes no timings. This file takes them from Table 1 of the Swann paper (Persinger 2002), an inference: point duration, gap and step are 1 ms, 1 ms and 20 to 34 ms (B1, T1), 1 ms, 1 ms and 100 to 240 ms (B2, T2), 3 ms, 3 s and 200 to 186 ms (B3, T3). The sign follows Richards 2002 (p.3-4 [673-674]: -10 means 100, 90, 80 ms); later papers reverse it (Tsang 2004 p.5 [1187]). Lab runs of the Shiva software used other tables (Saroka 2010 p.5 [470]; Collins 2014 p.40 [31]). Each configuration runs 5 min, with 2 min without field between them as in Richards 2002 (p.4 [674]); the Swann run had no intervals (Persinger 2002 p.1 [927]). Amygdala: this project's rising sweep with the 289 points of the Shiva signal (Saroka 2010 p.5 [470]); the point values were never published. The chirp phases play a plain 40 Hz sine, neither Murphy's modulated 40 Hz chirp nor the lab's frequency-modulated pattern of 849 points (Tsang 2004 p.5 [1187]). One coil per position instead of Shiva's coil pairs: timing kept, half the arc covered. persinger-swann-2002-table1 is the lab version. The lab used 2 to 5 uT, place not stated (Persinger 2002 p.4 [930]), and 5 to 10 uT 'adjacent to the scalp' (Cook 1999 p.2 [62]). This program's setting is the peak field 20 mm in front of each coil. Murphy says Swann 'experienced a clear remote viewing' in the final phase; the paper says he 'began to perceive the three experimenters, outside of the chamber as skeletons' (Persinger 2002 p.8 [934]): one subject, no sham. Independent sham-controlled tests of God-Helmet-type fields found no field effect (Granqvist 2005, double-blind; Gendle & McGrath 2012, where the experimenter knew the condition). Not for people with epilepsy; stop if distressed.
setting: Dark, acoustically silent room, eyes covered, seated and relaxed without meditating or falling asleep. For effects during the session Murphy recommends the highest Shiva setting (92%) in sensory deprivation, 'especially silence'; the lab subjects sat blindfolded in an acoustic chamber.
schedule: At most once a week; never on consecutive days, and not back to back with the Persinger Session.

phases.name: 1 Amygdala (B1): 1-ms points, 1-ms gaps, 20 to 34 ms per coil
2 Amygdala (B2): 1-ms points, 1-ms gaps, 100 to 240 ms per coil
3 Amygdala (B3): 3-ms points, 3-s gaps, 200 to 186 ms per coil
4 Chirp, steady 40 Hz (T1): 1-ms points, 20 to 34 ms per coil
5 Chirp (T2): 1-ms points, 100 to 240 ms per coil
6 Chirp (T3): 3-ms points, 3-s gaps, 200 to 186 ms per coil
